docs: state what eyeball is, how it is built, and how it is written

Four documents before any code, in a deliberate order. product.md answers
what the thing does and architecture.md is derived from it, and neither
could have been written second: choosing between a server-rendered surface
and a client one depends on whether a comment has to survive being offline,
which is a product question wearing an engineering costume.

conventions.md and voice.md exist because a rule that is only understood
gets violated. Both mark which of their rules a machine can check, so the
checks written later cite a rule instead of inventing one at the moment of
enforcing it.
